brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.

requirements.requirement: A utensil holder: holds kitchen utensils standing upright
requirements.evidence: A fork (prop:1) and a knife (prop:3) stand upright in bin 0,0,0 and a spoon (prop:2) in bin 1,0,0. No warnings, and the look view shows all three.
There are two full-depth bins, bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full, in two cells bolted together.
I chose bins with no drain holes, which helps, but how well the printed plastic holds water depends on the material and print settings. The configurator can't check that.
Whether it survives a dishwasher depends on the printing material and print settings. The configurator knows nothing about heat or detergent resistance, so this can't be met or verified here.

finish.summary: I built a two-bin utensil holder, but I can't confirm the waterproof or dishwasher-safe parts of the brief. It's two full hex cells side by side, each holding a full-depth bin with a solid floor (no drain holes). All open faces are capped and the joint between the cells is bolted, so it's 14 parts in total. For display, a fork and a knife stand upright in one bin and a spoon in the other. check_build found no rule issues and no mesh collisions. The configurator only checks fit and collisions. Whether the holder is waterproof or dishwasher safe depends on the printing material and how it's printed, and nothing here can check either.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
